summary: Explains the need for a new pair of IANA Diameter Command Codes for a vendor-specific application, the ITU-T Q.3303.3 Rw interface, which carries requests to authorize network quality-of-service resources and policy enforcement. This is an informational document.

plainLanguage.summary: The Rw interface exchanges policy decisions about network resources and quality of service. This memo records Diameter identifiers for that application.

subtitle: Diameter identifiers for the ITU-T Rw policy-enforcement application.

tldr.problem: The ITU-T Rw interface needs Diameter identifiers for requests and responses about network QoS resources and policy enforcement.
tldr.mechanism: The memo records an application identifier, command code 315, and vendor-specific AVP codes for the ITU-T application.
tldr.outcome: It documents the Diameter codes associated with the ITU-T Rw interface and says the base Diameter security considerations apply.

today: RFC 5431 is an Informational memo describing Diameter identifiers for the ITU-T Rw application. The unit metadata lists no update or replacement.

sections.title: Policy Decisions over the Rw Interface
sections.content:
The Rw interface carries policy decisions between a Policy Decision Point and a Policy Enforcement Point. The RFC says it can carry authorized admission decisions to an enforcement point or let the enforcement point request authorization.

The information includes resource requests, QoS handling, gate control, address mapping for NAT traversal, and resource-use reports. The application builds on the Diameter Base protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: One network component decides what resources a flow may use, and another applies that decision. The Rw interface carries those decisions and related requests.

sections.title: Application and Command Identifiers
sections.content:
The memo records vendor-specific Application Identifier 16777256 for ITU-T Rw. It lists command code 315 for Policy-Install-Request and Policy-Install-Answer, abbreviated PIR and PIA.

It also lists AVP codes 1010 through 1018 in the ITU-T vendor-ID namespace 11502. The referenced ITU-T recommendation contains detailed AVP definitions.
sections.plainLanguage: The application has a vendor-specific identifier, and its policy-install request and answer use command code 315. The memo also identifies a range of vendor-specific attribute codes.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says the application builds on the Diameter Base protocol and that its security considerations apply. It says no additional extensions beyond those security mechanisms are required.

This document describes identifiers for the interface; the detailed policy protocol is specified by the referenced ITU-T recommendation.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo relies on the security mechanisms of the Diameter Base protocol. It does not add new security extensions.
